worked_example.reading: the shared words -- the, committee, rates, and -- carry a small IDF and almost no weight; what survives is each sentence's own vocabulary, which is why the cosine between d1 and d2 falls from 0.571 on raw counts to 0.152 on TF-IDF

embeddings.out_of_vocabulary_note: A word that appears fewer than min_count times in the training window has no vector at all. That is a property of the method, not a defect of this run, and the analogy table says so.

contract.produced_by: session05_measure.py, outside this module and outside this process
contract.format: CSV with a header row and either the columns date,variant,label or the columns date,score
contract.date: YYYY-MM-DD, matching a statement date in the corpus
contract.variant: A is the frozen prompt and the one this interface reads by default; B, C and D exist on a subsample so prompt sensitivity can be measured
contract.label: HAWKISH, NEUTRAL or DOVISH, mapped here to +1, 0 and -1
contract.score: if the file carries a numeric column instead, it is used as is, on the same orientation as the other three signals: positive hawkish, negative dovish
contract.missing: a date absent from the file scores as nan and is dropped by `validate_signal`
contract.why_here: so the notebook can validate all four signals through one function; this module never calls a model, never touches the network, and never writes the score file
